ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: This account is overwhelmingly rank-constrained, not budget-constrained. The three in-scope non-brand Search campaigns are sitting at only 5–7% search impression share while losing 93–95% to rank with 0% lost to budget, and budgets are only ~56–59% utilized. Auction evidence confirms you’re consistently being pushed down-page (self top-of-page rate 15.2% vs competitors 73.2%) even when you do enter auctions, which aligns with the very high lost-to-rank figures and low non-brand ROAS.
notable_patterns: Non-brand Search is demand-rich but suppressed by rank: Auto IS 6% with 94% lost to rank; Home IS 5% with 95% lost to rank; Life IS 7% with 93% lost to rank — all with 0% lost to budget and only ~56–59% budget utilization.

You have high-intent keywords with strong quality signals but still almost no coverage: e.g., "auto insurance germany" (QS 9.0) at 5% IS with 95% lost to rank; "home insurance cost" (QS 8.5) at 5.5% IS with 94.5% lost to rank; "car insurance quote" (QS 8.0) at 6% IS with 94% lost to rank.

Competitive pressure is structurally keeping you off the top positions: avg position-above rate 85.4% and self top-of-page rate 15.2% vs competitors 73.2% (notably Nordkreuz Assurance position-above 96.5% and competitor top-of-page 82.6%).

A material share of query volume is being wasted on competitor-brand ‘zero-click’ traffic: 35,700 competitor-brand zero-click impressions and 48.3% of search-term impressions coming from zero-click competitor terms, while only one competitor term is shown converting ("nordkreuz insurance quote": 1.0 conv).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Coverage is extremely low (6% impression share) with demand blocked almost entirely by rank (94% lost to rank, 0% lost to budget) despite only 57.2% budget utilization. This is consistent with auction results showing you rarely reach top-of-page (self top-of-page generally 12–18% vs competitors 66–83%).
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Restructure and bid into the highest-intent auto terms (e.g., "auto insurance germany", "car insurance quote") with top-of-page-focused bids/targets and tighter query controls to avoid competitor-brand zero-click leakage.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: This campaign has the worst efficiency signals paired with severe rank loss: 5% impression share and 95% lost to rank with 0% lost to budget, plus a very low avg quality score (4.1). The combination suggests ad/landing relevance issues are compounding rank loss rather than budget being the limiter.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize quality-score recovery (intent-segmented ad groups, stronger RSAs/LP alignment) and prune/negate low-intent informational queries driving costly conversions (e.g., "home insurance claims process" QS 4.0; €2,248.95 spend; €244.45 cost/conv).

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Life is heavily suppressed by rank (7% impression share; 93% lost to rank; 0% lost to budget) and has an extremely low avg quality score (2.0), indicating relevance/landing experience is likely the dominant constraint. With ROAS at 0.89, scaling without fixing rank/quality will likely amplify inefficiency.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Rebuild the life campaign around fewer, higher-intent themes (e.g., "life insurance comparison" QS 7.5 but only 7% IS) and correct the quality-score drivers before attempting more aggressive scale.

recommendation_cards.title: Win back non-brand impression share by forcing top-of-page eligibility on your best high-intent terms
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Your non-brand campaigns are barely entering auctions: Auto IS 6% (94% lost to rank), Home IS 5% (95% lost to rank), Life IS 7% (93% lost to rank), all with 0% lost to budget and only ~56–59% budget utilization. At the same time, you have high-quality, high-intent terms still stuck at ~5–7% IS: "auto insurance germany" (QS 9.0; 5% IS; 95% lost to rank) and "car insurance quote" (QS 8.0; 6% IS; 94% lost to rank).
recommended_steps: Segment out these high-intent keywords into dedicated ad groups/campaign segments (Auto/Home/Life) so bids and messaging can be set specifically for top-of-page entry.
Increase bids/targets specifically on the segmented high-intent set until you see meaningful reduction in lost-to-rank (do not raise budgets first; budgets aren’t binding at ~56–59% utilization).
Use competitive positioning as the guardrail: you’re currently top-of-page only 15.2% vs competitors 73.2%, so optimize for top-of-page eligibility before expanding keyword lists.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share on the segmented high-intent keywords moving from ~5–7% toward 15%+ while lost-to-rank drops from ~93–95% toward <80%.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix quality-score collapse in Home/Life by rebuilding intent-based structure and landing-message alignment
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Home Insurance has avg quality score 4.1 and Life Insurance is at 2.0, alongside extreme lost-to-rank (95% and 93%). This points to relevance/landing experience issues amplifying rank loss, not budget caps (0% lost to budget in both).
recommended_steps: Rebuild Home and Life into tighter intent clusters (e.g., ‘quote/vergleich/kosten’ vs ‘definition/claims/how-to’) with distinct ad copy and the most relevant landing page per cluster.

For Life in particular (avg QS 2.0), pause or heavily downbid broad informational themes and keep only high-intent comparatives (e.g., keep/expand around "life insurance comparison" (QS 7.5) while isolating it from low-intent traffic).
Refresh the weakest ad set first: 1 of 5 ads is rated only “Average”; ensure each rebuilt cluster has tailored headlines/descriptions aligned to the query intent and landing content.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Avg quality score in Home from 4.1 toward 6.0+ and Life from 2.0 toward 5.0+, along with improved top-of-page rate from 15.2% toward 25%+.

recommendation_cards.title: Stop paying for competitor-brand ‘zero-click’ query volume with tight negatives and targeting boundaries
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Competitor-brand zero-click impressions are 35,700 and these zero-click competitor terms account for 48.3% of search-term impressions. Only one competitor term is shown converting ("nordkreuz insurance quote": 1.0 conv), implying most competitor-brand exposure is wasted while you’re already rank-constrained on your own high-intent non-brand terms.
recommended_steps: Add exact/phrase negatives for the non-converting competitor brands listed (e.g., "bluewave insurance", "harborline mutual", "crestfield direct") in non-brand campaigns/ad groups where they appear.
If you intentionally conquest, isolate it into its own segment with capped bids and separate measurement so it cannot cannibalize rank/budget from core non-brand terms.
Reallocate the freed auction participation toward your proven high-intent generics (e.g., "auto insurance germany", "car insurance quote", "home insurance cost").
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from competitor zero-click terms dropping from 48.3% to <20%, while non-brand generic impression share rises (Auto 6% -> 10%+ initially).

recommendation_cards.title: Cut or quarantine the worst ‘low-quality, high-cost’ queries to prevent rank and ROAS drag
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Several low-QS keywords are consuming meaningful spend at extreme costs: "insurance company phone number" (QS 3.0; €2,605.80 spend; €1,371.47 cost/conv) and "what is life insurance" (QS 4.5; €858.99 spend; €613.56 cost/conv). These patterns are consistent with informational/service queries that rarely produce profitable insurance leads, and they can also dilute campaign-level relevance signals.
recommended_steps: Add negatives or move these themes into a separate ‘service/info’ segment with very conservative bids and dedicated messaging (or pause if lead quality is poor).
Prioritize removal/quarantine in Life/Home first given their very low avg QS (2.0 and 4.1) and already weak ROAS (0.89 and 0.75).
Review the actual matched queries behind these keywords and negate the recurring modifiers (e.g., phone number, claims process, what is).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Cost/conv on the affected segments decreasing by 30%+ while overall non-brand lost-to-rank improves (fewer low-quality auctions entered).

recommendation_cards.title: Resolve internal negative conflicts that are blocking your own captured intent (without reopening low-quality traffic)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The negative-keyword conflicts report shows 3,810 estimated blocked impressions. The biggest is negative "free" blocking "insurance quote calculator free" in Dynamic Search Ads - Long Tail (3,400 blocked impressions). There’s also "jobs" blocking "insurance agent jobs near me insurance quote" (410 blocked impressions).
recommended_steps: Keep the protective intent of negatives, but refine from broad to more precise: allow the ‘calculator’ intent while still excluding true freebie seekers (e.g., negate ‘download free’, ‘template free’, etc. rather than blocking all ‘free’ if you want this traffic).
For the ‘jobs’ conflict, keep ‘jobs’ as a negative but add stricter keyword/targeting so employment queries don’t match your quote-focused ad groups in the first place.
Only reopen these conflicts in a tightly controlled test segment so it doesn’t worsen already-low non-brand ROAS.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Incremental conversions from the re-enabled traffic with guardrails (e.g., maintain cost/conv within 20% of non-brand baseline while monitoring search-term quality).

already_working: Budgets are not limiting delivery right now: every campaign shows 0% impression share lost to budget and budget utilization is only ~51–59% (e.g., Auto 57.2%, Home 58.5%, Life 56.2%).

Brand Search is comparatively healthy on coverage (85% impression share) and strong profitability (ROAS 4.7 on €34,552.32 spend), so the bigger upside is clearly in fixing non-brand rank/quality rather than reallocating away from brand.

Ad creation isn’t the primary bottleneck: 80% of ads are rated Good/Excellent (3 Excellent, 1 Good), suggesting the bigger issues are rank pressure, query mix, and quality-score/landing alignment in non-brand segments.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: The account’s non-brand Search is being structurally shut out by rank at the same time the German insurance search market is accelerating. Third-party data shows Germany insurance search spend is up +18% QoQ while query demand is up +12% QoQ, and the vertical-average impression share benchmark is 21%—far above your current 5–7%. Meanwhile, competitors are visibly investing in Search (and multi-channel) with meaningful spend share and large creative volumes, which will keep auctions expensive/top-of-page harder to win if you don’t address rank (bids + Quality Score drivers) immediately. Demand on your exact high-intent themes is also rising (e.g., “car insurance quote” +28% and “home insurance cost” +19%), so every week you delay compounds missed high-intent coverage while budgets remain underutilized.

In a rank-constrained account, rising competitive spend directly worsens your ability to enter/top auctions unless you fix rank now (top-of-page eligibility via bids + QS improvements). Also sets a benchmark (21% avg IS) showing how far below-normal your 5–7% IS is.
